title: Overlay media queue response (PRF-02 slice 7, catalogue module #20)
description: The overlay-facing projection of a channel's live media queue rotation, scoped by the overlay session token. CREATOR-ONLY (owner decision, 2026-09-17; register row MED-20): the creator queues their own media and viewers cannot submit -- there is no submission endpoint, no approval queue and no viewer-facing write surface anywhere in this product, and this response is read-only by construction. AT MOST TWO ENTRIES, labelled 'current' and 'next', and nothing else: 12.7's Overlay row authorises 'current and next alert state' in those exact words, and this reuses the identical bound apps/web/app/overlay/canvas/modules/support-theater-module.ts already established for this codebase rather than inventing a queue-depth number -- there is no aggregate count of how many items are queued anywhere in this schema. Metadata only (19.1): storageUrl and thumbnailUrl point at an already-hosted GCS/CDN asset, never bytes, and MED-21 records the bytea path this module never uses as legacy. mimeType is a closed allow-list (9.1.1) -- no text/html, no image/svg+xml (inline script), no application/* of any kind -- so nothing on this path can ever carry a script, an iframe or a stylesheet onto the Master Canvas. No item id, no submitter identity and no viewer identity exists on this schema at all -- not withheld, but absent, so nothing here can correlate one visit to another. An empty array is what an unrecognised, expired, revoked or foreign overlay token returns, and also what a channel with nothing live in rotation returns -- both mean paint nothing.

queueSlot.description: Exactly two possible values, and at most one row of each. There is no third slot and no aggregate queue-depth count anywhere in this schema.

mimeType.description: A closed allow-list (9.1.1). No text/html, no image/svg+xml, no application/* of any kind -- nothing here can ever describe a document capable of executing code on the Canvas.

storageUrl.description: Metadata only (19.1): an already-hosted GCS/CDN asset. No bytes are ever returned on this path.

durationMs.description: Null for an image. The maximum here is PostgreSQL integer's own storage range; the actual governing cap is a CONFIGURED-BUT-UNSET deployment value enforced at enqueue time, never invented by this contract.
